summary: Ngan-che Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong (attested 2007), where they were supervised by Jing Yin and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

Ngawang Jinpa studied at Drepung Loseling College and worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held a post as professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling (attested 1995), and taught Kevin Alan Vose and Lobsang Tendzin.
Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Ngawang Jorden has held posts at Harvard University (attested 1999) and Sakya College, and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.
Ngawang Lek Shé Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Ngawang Nyima, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Trijang Rinpoche. He taught Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and Thubten Jigme Norbu.

Ngawang Samten (b. 1956) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at CIHTS and Ganden Monastery, he directed CIHTS (attested 1990–2019), served as Principal Teacher at the Vajrayana Institute, and held visiting posts at Smith, Hampshire, Amherst, and Tasmania.
Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Shenphen Nangwa.

Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery and under Yeshe Paldrup, Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen, later teaching numerous disciples.
Nguyen Thi Tuyet is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who received a PhD from Punjabi University (attested 2012) under Inder Mohan Singh, having also studied under Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.
Nguyen Thi Xinh is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).
Nguyen Van Hoa, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, completed a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under the doctoral supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.
Nguyen Van Thuong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Delhi under MA supervisor Karam Tej Singh Sarao.

Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and under teachers including Lianju Xia, Hsu Yun, and Gongga Rinpoche. In Buddhist studies, he headed the Central Broadcasting Station and was a professor at BUPT (~1953).
Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) studied at Rissho University (1912), Taisho, Koyasan, Horyuji Kangakuin, and Kennin-ji. Active in religious and Buddhist studies, he founded Nipponzan-Myohoji.

Nicholas Dirks (b. 1950) studied at Wesleyan and the University of Chicago (~1972–1981). Working in Indology and history/archaeology, he held posts at Caltech (~1986–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).

Nicholas Justin Allen (1939–2020) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Oxford under Rodney Needham, he lectured at Durham (1972–1976) and served at Oxford as Lecturer (1976) and Reader (1997) in the Social Anthropology of South Asia.

Nicholas Poppe (1897–1991), a linguist and Central Asian specialist, studied at Saint Petersburg State University. He was a professor at Saint Petersburg (1923, 1925–1941) and later served on the faculty at the University of Washington (1949–1968).

Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947), active in history, archaeology, and Central Asian studies, studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts. He directed the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts and founded the Urusvati Institute.
Nicholas Witkowski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at Stanford University in 2015 and served as a research fellow at the University of Tokyo (attested 2017).
Nicholson T. Collier is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.
